subject: Confidentiality & trade-secret damages: carve-out language discussion

Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: carve-out for trade-secret/confidentiality breaches from liability cap

Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal has pushed back on our standard liability language because it would leave us without a remedy if our trade secrets or other high-sensitivity IP are disclosed. We need a carve-out to the liability cap for confidentiality breaches involving trade secrets (and related forensic/remediation costs).

Suggested quick language to insert under Limitation of Liability: 
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, damages arising from unauthorized acquisition, disclosure or use of Customer trade secrets, or awarded by a court for breach of confidentiality obligations, and reasonable costs of forensic investigation and notification shall not be subject to the limitation of liability."

We attached a redline of your MSA with our suggested insertion (MSA_redlines_v3.docx). Can Redwood confirm acceptance or propose a counter? This is a blocker for procurement. Happy to hop on a call if useful.

—Jordan

Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for trade-secret/confidentiality breaches from liability cap

Thanks, team. I reviewed Jordan's proposed insertion and drafted a response that protects Redwood's operational exposure while addressing Stellaris' core concern. High-level: Redwood will agree to a targeted carve-out for confidentiality breaches that are (i) trade-secret misappropriation or (ii) court-awarded damages for breach of confidentiality, and that also covers reasonable forensic investigation and notification costs.

Proposed compromise language (for insertion into Section 9.x Limitation of Liability):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in this Section shall not apply to: (a) amounts awarded by a court or arbitrator for breach of the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section X; (b) proven misappropriation of Customer trade secrets by Redwood or its personnel; and (c) reasonable and documented costs incurred by Customer for forensic investigation, notification, and remediation directly resulting from such breach (collectively, the "Confidentiality Carve-Out").

The Confidentiality Carve-Out shall apply only where Customer: (i) notifies Redwood in writing within thirty (30) days of becoming aware of the alleged breach; (ii) provides reasonable documentation of the alleged misappropriation or disclosure (including forensic evidence or court process); and (iii) grants Redwood a commercially reasonable opportunity to investigate and, if applicable, mitigate the incident.

For clarity, ordinary negligence-based confidentiality incidents that do not involve demonstrable misappropriation of trade secrets or court-awarded damages shall remain subject to the general limitation of liability.

Rationale: this preserves Stellaris' right to full recovery for the most severe confidentiality failures (trade-secret theft, court-ordered damages) while limiting open-ended exposure for speculative or low-impact incidents. We can consider a narrower drafting if Stellaris requires removal of the "willful"/"proven" qualifier, but Redwood would need the documentation/forensic gate above.

I've attached a small redline and a short forensic-evidence-process PDF that explains the types of artifacts (log exports, signed attestations, chain-of-custody) we will typically rely on.

Open to a quick call this afternoon to walk through.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Transactions
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@stellarishealth.com>

Date: Thu, 23 Feb 2028 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for trade-secret/confidentiality breaches from liability cap

Karthik —

Thanks for the thoughtful compromise. A couple quick points from our side:
- Stellaris cannot accept a solution that requires a court determination as the only trigger for unlimited recovery; that would leave us without an interim remedy in the event of clear exfiltration.
- Removing the "proven"/"willful" burden is important for our board and procurement — we need the carve-out to apply where there is reasonable evidence of misappropriation and documented forensic findings, not only post-judgment.

We are comfortable with the notice/forensic cooperation gate you proposed. Can we tweak language so that the carve-out triggers on "demonstrated misappropriation based on reasonable forensic evidence, or final adjudication awarding damages for breach of confidentiality"? That gives Redwood the chance to investigate but removes the requirement for a court judgment in every case.

Also, can Redwood confirm it will indemnify Stellaris for third-party claims arising from such misappropriation (standard mutual indemnity carve-out)? That is another procurement ask.

If we can land on wording like the line above I can escalate to procurement and legal and (likely) get green light. I'm available at 12:30 PT for a quick 20-min call.

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Dir., Contracts & Compliance
Stellaris Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: carve-out for trade-secret/confidentiality breaches from liability cap

Jordan —

We had a quick internal alignment with Product and Security this morning and believe we can accept the carve-out with the tweaks you proposed, subject to two commercial backstops: (1) the carve-out should be limited to incidents where there is demonstrable forensic evidence of exfiltration/misappropriation (as you suggested), and (2) Redwood asks that, for negligence-level incidents that fall short of willful misappropriation but still meet the forensic threshold, parties agree to an aggregate confidentiality-related cap of $15,000,000 for all such claims arising from the incident (this preserves a backstop for extreme, but not unlimited, exposure).

Proposed final text for execution: 

"Notwithstanding any other provision, the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in this Agreement shall not apply to: (a) amounts finally awarded by a court or arbitrator for breach of the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section X; or (b) amounts resulting from demonstrated misappropriation of Customer trade secrets or unauthorized acquisition or disclosure of Customer Confidential Information, in each case evidenced by reasonable and documented forensic artifacts (including but not limited to log exports, forensic reports, and chain-of-custody records) (collectively, the "Confidentiality Carve-Out").

Where damages under clause (b) are based on negligence rather than willful misconduct, the parties agree that Redwood's aggregate liability for such confidentiality-related damages arising from the same incident shall not exceed Fifteen Million US Dollars (USD 15,000,000). The Confidentiality Carve-Out also includes reasonable and documented costs for forensic investigation, notification, and remediation directly resulting from such breach.

The Confidentiality Carve-Out shall apply only where Customer: (i) notifies Redwood in writing within thirty (30) days of becoming aware of the alleged breach; (ii) provides reasonable and documented forensic evidence of the alleged misappropriation or disclosure; and (iii) provides Redwood a commercially reasonable opportunity to investigate and mitigate the incident.

Finally, Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims arising directly from an event that falls within the Confidentiality Carve-Out, subject to the procedures set forth in Section Y (Indemnification).

If that language is acceptable I'll ask Contracts to prepare an updated MSA for signature (we'll incorporate the redline and the limited $15M backstop). Thanks for moving quickly on this — glad we could find middle ground.

—Karthik

Senior Counsel, Transactions
Redwood Inference
